entries.name: Find a gift by recipient and budget
entries.visitor_need: Choose an appropriate gift without browsing every product.
entries.difference: Recipient and budget change the recommendation; out-of-stock results need a useful fallback.
acceptance: Exercise each recipient/budget route and fallback.
A recommendation remains available without giving contact details.

entries.name: Find products for a small space
entries.visitor_need: Find products that fit a small room or balcony.
entries.difference: Available space and intended use determine a shortlist, with a visible reason for the match.
acceptance: Test the smallest-space branch and no-match route.
Compare listed dimensions with actual product dimensions.

entries.name: Choose a starter or experienced kit
entries.visitor_need: Choose equipment suitable for current experience.
entries.difference: Experience gates follow-up questions; revising an earlier answer removes irrelevant later answers.
acceptance: Back changes both the follow-up screen and recommendation.
No unsupported safety or performance claims.

entries.name: Compare product materials
entries.visitor_need: Understand material tradeoffs before buying.
entries.difference: A concise comparison leads to specifications rather than another collection announcement.
acceptance: Both materials have readable tradeoffs at 320px.
Destination provides care, dimensions and material details.

entries.name: Ask for a material sample
entries.visitor_need: Request help obtaining a fabric or finish sample.
entries.difference: Capture material interest and contact details; avoid collecting addresses or claiming dispatch.
acceptance: Sample selection reaches the saved enquiry.
Acknowledgement promises a reply about samples, never shipment.

entries.name: Plan a bulk gift order
entries.visitor_need: Ask whether a business can supply a group gift order.
entries.difference: Quantity range changes the conversation; no invented quantity field or automatic quote.
acceptance: Quantity ranges use supported choice fields.
No price, availability or delivery promise before confirmation.

entries.name: Ask about a custom product
entries.visitor_need: Check whether a product can be personalised.
entries.difference: Personalisation type and follow-up needs differ from general product advice.
acceptance: Request type survives retry.
The next action explains how specifications will be collected.

entries.name: Choose a collection for shop news
entries.visitor_need: Receive updates about a chosen product category.
entries.difference: Saved category preference must correspond to an actual follow-up process.
acceptance: Preference and consent persist in the same lead.
Setup explains that capture alone does not create provider segmentation.

entries.name: Prepare measurements before buying
entries.visitor_need: Check doorway and room measurements before ordering furniture.
entries.difference: Delivery access checklist is distinct from clothing size or product care guidance.
acceptance: Resource covers both access and placement measurements.
All units and diagrams agree.

entries.name: Explain collection from a local shop
entries.visitor_need: Find pickup location, hours and collection terms.
entries.difference: Pickup information uses a merchant-authored destination and makes no delivery claim.
acceptance: Hours and location appear on the destination.
Bar label, heading and action stay balanced at 320px.

entries.name: Offer product help near the basket
entries.visitor_need: Resolve a product question before ordering.
entries.difference: A support enquiry placed near the basket; it must not imply automatic cart attachment.
acceptance: Placement does not interrupt checkout or cover its controls.
Enquiry asks enough context without claiming knowledge of cart contents.

entries.name: Explain return conditions before purchase
entries.visitor_need: Understand the merchant’s return process and exclusions.
entries.difference: Reduces purchase uncertainty with actual policy details, separate from shipping terms.
acceptance: Merchant supplies the actual policy; no invented consumer-law claims.
Policy is accessible without signup.

entries.name: Find the right service
entries.visitor_need: Identify an appropriate service before asking for a quote.
entries.difference: Project type and stage route to specific service explanations; unknown needs get a human-help fallback.
acceptance: Every answer combination has a useful outcome.
Results suggest services without quoting a price or confirming eligibility.

entries.name: Choose a project’s next step
entries.visitor_need: Know whether to plan, consult or request an estimate.
entries.difference: Project stage drives guidance rather than simply collecting another enquiry.
acceptance: Early-stage visitors can read guidance without signup.
Back and changed answers update results.

entries.name: Find service area information
entries.visitor_need: Check whether a business serves the visitor’s area.
entries.difference: A coverage-page handoff; do not pretend unsupported postcode validation exists.
acceptance: Coverage and exceptions are explicit on the linked page.
No false supported-address confirmation.

entries.name: Request a non-urgent repair assessment
entries.visitor_need: Describe the category of repair and arrange follow-up.
entries.difference: Service type and first-contact workflow differ from a general estimate; no emergency-response promise.
acceptance: Category reaches the saved enquiry.
Acknowledgement distinguishes a request from a confirmed visit.

entries.name: Ask about training for a team
entries.visitor_need: Discuss training for a group rather than an individual learner.
entries.difference: Team-size bands qualify the request; no new custom field type required.
acceptance: Group size options remain readable on phones.
No automatic enrolment or confirmed date.

entries.name: Compare service packages
entries.visitor_need: Understand what different service packages include.
entries.difference: Package comparison needs aligned inclusions and a clear next step.
acceptance: Long inclusions wrap without misaligning comparison rows.
All displayed packages and terms exist on the destination.

entries.name: Prepare for a service consultation
entries.visitor_need: Gather basic information before an initial consultation.
entries.difference: Preparation checklist must reduce follow-up work and avoid requesting sensitive records in the form.
acceptance: Resource states what to prepare and how the business will follow up.
Immediate access and local resource-mail handoff work.

entries.name: Explore a business open day
entries.visitor_need: See an open-day agenda and registration details.
entries.difference: Event explanation has a real date and venue; registration remains on the configured destination.
acceptance: Date, venue and accessibility information are present.
No claim that clicking completes registration.

entries.name: Choose a reading path
entries.visitor_need: Find a beginner or deeper reading sequence.
entries.difference: Topic plus familiarity produces an ordered path rather than a single article suggestion.
acceptance: Each path has useful accessible content.
No signup required to open recommendations.

entries.name: Send an editorial question
entries.visitor_need: Ask the editorial team about a topic.
entries.difference: Supported topic choice plus contact details starts a reply; do not invent a long-message field.
acceptance: Topic choice is saved; no public posting or publication claim.
Acknowledgement explains the editorial follow-up.

entries.name: Start a multi-part article series
entries.visitor_need: Find the beginning of a series when arriving midway.
entries.difference: Contextual navigation to part one is different from a generic related-article card.
acceptance: Link opens the correct first part.
Placement does not obscure the current article.

entries.name: Choose a brief or detailed editorial letter
entries.visitor_need: Choose the amount of reading to receive.
entries.difference: Format preference needs an explicit editorial/provider mapping; it is not automatic segmentation.
acceptance: Both preferences survive capture and retry.
Merchant has a follow-up process for each choice.
